memories.author: D05
memories.text: Migraine with chronic tension-type features and episodic urticaria. Patient reports throbbing bifrontal headaches 4 days/week, associated photophobia, and daily pruritic wheals on trunk and limbs. Examination: afebrile, BP 118/72, pulse 78, no focal neurology; skin shows scattered wheals, no angioedema. Neurological exam normal. Plan: start prophylactic propranolol, acute sumatriptan, levocetirizine for urticaria, and check vitamin D.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Propranolol 40 mg OD
Sumatriptan 50 mg SOS
Topiramate 25 mg HS
Naproxen 500 mg SOS
Levocetirizine 5 mg OD
Cetirizine 10 mg HS
Cholecalciferol 60000 IU once weekly for 8 weeks, then 1000 IU OD

memories.author: patient
memories.text: I’ve been taking the medicines as prescribed. The hives are much less itchy and I only get a small bump now and then. Headaches still happen about three times a week, sometimes I need sumatriptan. No side effects noticed.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Migraine: frequency reduced to 2-3 days/week, mild‑moderate intensity, sumatriptan used twice in past month. Urticaria: occasional wheals, no angioedema. Vitamin D still low on recent labs. Examination: vitals stable, skin clear, no neurological deficits. Assessment: migraine partially controlled (ACT score 16), urticaria improving, vitamin D deficiency persistent. Plan: continue propranolol, increase topiramate to 50 mg HS for migraine prophylaxis, keep levocetirizine, continue vitamin D repletion.

memories.text: Migraine: headache days down to 1-2/week, ACT score 20 (well controlled). Urticaria: rare wheals, no distress. Vitamin D now sufficient. Examination: vitals normal, skin clear, no neurological findings. Assessment: migraine well controlled, urticaria controlled, vitamin D replete. Plan: taper high‑dose vitamin D to maintenance 1000 IU OD, reduce topiramate to 25 mg HS due to mild paresthesia, continue propranolol and levocetirizine.
